title.narrative: UNODC (2014-2019) Criminal Justice - Nat Integr Progr for ETI Sub Prog. 2
UNODC (2014-2019) Criminal Justice - Nat Integr Progr for ETI Sub Prog. 2

description.narrative:
The overall objective of this sub-programme is to support the GoEs justice reform efforts towards an effective and efficient criminal justice system to improve effectiveness, accessibility, accountability, transparency and fairness of the justice system.
The expected outcomes are:
1) the sustainability of a broad-based National Crime Prevention Strategy and Action Plan 2) the adoption of professional standards, systems and legislative and administrative measures 3) the adoption of standards and strategies for greater efficiency, effectiveness and accountability of the prosecution 4) the implementation of programmes to strengthen humane and secure imprisonment and alternative programmes 5) support to victims and witnesses 6) the adoption of programmes to improve the protection of children in conflict with the law and 7) the access to justice for indigents, in particular vulnerable and at risk-groups

Ett effektivt, tillgängligt och rättvist rättssystem är essentiellt för god samhällsstyrning, genom att upprätthålla lagefterlevnad och etablera en stabil och förutsäglig miljö för investerare, ekonomisk tillväxt och fattigdomsbekämpning. Delprogrammet rörande det straffrättsliga systemet och det Nationella Integrerade Programmet för Etiopiens (NPE) integritet ämnar stärka lagefterlevnaden genom att förebygga brott och att främja ett rättvist, humant och ansvarskyldigt straffrättsligt system. För att göra detta kommer UNODC att assistera och delge expertis till Etiopiens regering angående att utveckla en effektiv och ansvarsfull Nationell Brottsförebyggande Strategi och tillvägagångsplan. De kommer också att hjälpa till med kapacitetsutveckling av det straffrättsliga systemet så att det ska verka effektivare inom en rättstat, medan det främjar mänskliga rättigheter och skyddar utsatta samhällsgrupper. Sverige har beslutat, baserat på UNODC:s NPE och i linje med UNODC:s Regionala Program för Östafrika (2009-2015), att stödja de två nedanstående resultat inom NPE. Stödet utgår under de kommande tre åren och uppgår till totalt 12 MSEK. Utav dessa 12 MSEK kommer 2 MSEK att utbetalas 2014, 5 MSEK 2015 och 5 MSEK 2016.
1.Rättvisa för barn UNODC resultat 6: Etiopiens regering antar program för förbättrat skydd av barn som brutit mot lagen 2.Rättshjälp UNODC resultat 7: Etiopiens regering utökar program för förbättrad tillgång till rättssystemet för hjälpbehövande, speciellt utsatta och övriga riskgrupper. .

The present proposal falls under Sub-Programme 2 of the National Integrated Programme on Criminal Justice and Integrity, with a focus on strengthening the criminal justice system in Ethiopia. It is based on an assessment of the criminal justice system in Ethiopia which was undertaken by UNODC in 2011 following a request by the GoE. This assessment identified various areas that need to be addressed to support the Government’s reform efforts towards an effective and efficient criminal justice system, including the proposed interventions on strengthening justice for children (Outcome 6) and enhancing legal aid/access to justice (Outcome 7).
An efficient, accessible and fair justice system is essential for good governance, upholding the rule of law and establishing a stable and predictable environment for investments, economic growth and poverty reduction. The sub-programme on criminal justice and integrity of the National Integrated Programme for Ethiopia (NPE) seeks to strengthen the rule of law through the prevention of crime and the promotion of fair, humane and accountable criminal justice system. To do this, UNODC will assist and provide expertise to the Government of Ethiopia in developing an effective and responsible National Crime Prevention Strategy and Action Plan and to build the capacity of their criminal justice systems to operate more effectively within the framework of the rule of law, while promoting human rights and protecting vulnerable groups. Based on UNODC’s NPE, and in line with UNODC’s Regional Programme for Eastern Africa (2009-2015).

UNODC has worked with an increasing presence in Ethiopia since 1995. Sweden's contribution supported one of the five pillars of UNODC's regional programme for East Africa, known as "Promoting the Rule of Law and Human Security (2016-2021)". The Pillar supported by Sweden is mostly focusing on: Crime Prevention and Criminal Justice, namely "Criminal Justice - National Integrated Programme for Ethiopia Sub-Programme II". Sweden has been a long-term main donor supporting UNODC's Ethiopia Sub- Programme II, while the Government of Japan is supporting the other pillar of the UNODC country programme on Transformation, Peace and Security in the Horn of Africa (2020 - 2022). Sweden's support to this intervention was intended to strengthen the criminal justice system in order to operate more effectively within the framework of the rule of law, while promoting human rights and protecting vulnerable groups. The Sub-Programme II has contributed to build capacities and policy harmonization in the criminal justice system, while engaging with some of the major actors in the criminal justice sector, such as, the Federal Office of the Attorney General (now the Ministry of Justice), the Federal Police Commission (FPC), the Federal Prison Association (FPA) and the Federal Supreme Courts (FSC). As stated in the Final Project Evaluation, over seven years of Sweden's support to this programme has seen various results, of which some of the major ones can be summarised as follows:
- One of the main achievements of UNODC is in relation to developing capacities, prison training has been traditionally focused on security issues but UNODC through this programme has made it possible to include human rights and international conventions standards. The adoption of the international minimum standard of treatment of prisoners, Nelson Mandela Rules is an achievement on its own.
- UNODCs support to the Child Justice Project of the Federal Supreme Court was highly relevant in a context where many programs of support for vulnerable women and children that had been running for up to 15 years had been discontinued. The number of child friendly benches in courts, which include video and audio equipment to avoid physical contact between victims and perpetrators had fallen from over 100 to only one but with UNODCs assistance this has increased to eight.
- At the government request, a comprehensive set of legislation was reviewed by this programme to comply with international standards (such as, Trafficking and Smuggling of Migrants Law, Asset Recovery Law, Anti-terrorism Law, Firearms Law, Criminal Procedure Code, National Crime Prevention Strategy, National Legal Aid Strategy, National Child Justice Strategy, Prosecution Led Crime Investigation Law and others). Some of these draft legislation, including those on federal prisons and human trafficking were subsequently adopted by the Federal Parliament, while the enactment of others, such as the Criminal Procedure and Evidence Code is still pending. Although, it is important to note that the Federal Prisons Proclamation is limited to the 6 federal prisons of the country and there is a need to cascade the prison reform in the regional states, where more than 90% of the countrys prisons are found.
- Through this support, UNODC was able to establish ICT centre at the prison training centre, at the Federal Police University, Federal Justice Professionals Training Center, and at Amhara regional level prison. Beneficiaries have been introduced to the known UNODC Global learning modules and they have already received their corresponding certifications in different topics including Alternatives to Imprisonment for Women Offenders and the Nelson Mandela Rules.
- Regarding the National Crime Prevention Strategy and Action Plan, UNODC's support have been effective and is allowing the criminal justice actors to devise preventive measures to address the conditions in which crime occurs. The programme has also supported an inter-institutional initiative led by the Government to enhance the capacity of law enforcement to used technology in the process of investigation. As a result an Automated Biometric Identification System (ABIS) has been installed with in the law enforcement institutions to strengthen their capacities in conducting investigations.
- The program developed a component on Education for Justice, conducting webinars at universities and printing modules for law schools to integrate into their curriculum, which contributes to promoting education and awareness in criminal justice, aligning with the broader goal of improving access to justice and rule of law.
- Sweden's deep-dive analysis on institutional building of some of its contributions have revealed that UNODC's staff have built strong relationship with key interlocutors within the government. As such, embedding consulting staff within what has been traditionally known as 'sensitive' government bodies, has been appreciated. Moreover, UNODC has been appreciated for its efforts of contextualizing and tailoring to local needs various international standards for ease of domestication and implementation.
- Furthermore, over seven years of implementation of the program led to the sustained engagement with the various stakeholders of the criminal justice sector. Moreover, UNODC has improved its coordination, under the UN team to co-chair the Justice Working group with UNDP.
